checks.claim: A catch basin has a sump below its outlet pipe where sand and grit settle out.
checks.why: State stormwater manuals describe the sump below the outlet invert as the space where coarse sediment settles.

sources.title: Deep Sump Hooded Catch Basin (Connecticut Stormwater Manual)

checks.claim: A detention tank holds storm water and releases it slowly to the river.
checks.why: Detention stores runoff briefly and releases it through a small outlet to cut the peak flow downstream.

checks.claim: A flap gate opens when water flows out and is forced shut when the river is higher.
checks.why: Flap gates open and close on the water levels either side: open to pass runoff, shut when the receiving water is higher.

sources.title: Devices for retrofitting stormwater systems to reduce tidal flood impacts (NC State Extension)

checks.claim: Storm water pump stations lift water over a closed flap gate when the river is high.
checks.why: Pump station guidance and case studies: when high river levels close the gates, pumps discharge the inland runoff.

sources.title: Between a Rock and the Mississippi River (Stormwater)
